current_authoritative_paper.title: Beyond Artifacts: Real-Centric Envelope Modeling for Reliable AI-Generated Image Detection
current_authoritative_paper.authors: Ruiqi Liu; Yi Han; Zhengbo Zhang; Liwei Yao; Zhiyuan Yan; Jialiang Shen; Zhijin Chen; Boyi Sun; Lubin Weng; Jing Dong; Yan Wang; Shu Wu
current_authoritative_paper.abstract: The rapid progress of generative models has intensified the need for reliable and robust detection under real-world conditions. However, existing detectors often overfit to generator-specific artifacts and remain highly sensitive to real-world degradations. As generative architectures evolve and images undergo multi-round cross-platform sharing and post-processing (chain degradations), these artifact cues become obsolete and harder to detect. To address this, we propose Real-centric Envelope Modeling (REM), a new paradigm that shifts detection from learning generator artifacts to modeling the robust distribution of real images. REM introduces feature-level perturbations in self-reconstruction to generate near-real samples, and employs an envelope estimator with cross-domain consistency to learn a boundary enclosing the real image manifold. We further build RealChain, a comprehensive benchmark covering both open-source and commercial generators with simulated real-world degradation. Across eight benchmark evaluations, REM achieves an average improvement of 7.5% over state-of-the-art methods, and notably maintains exceptional generalization on the severely degraded RealChain benchmark, establishing a solid foundation for synthetic image detection under real-world conditions. The code and the RealChain benchmark will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the paper.

local_search.interpretation: Magic-byte PDF/gzip search, SHA de-duplication and first-two-page exact identity inspection found no usable R034 complete manuscript. Historical compressed metadata was not treated as a complete paper. The raw receipt has a leftover AncesTree word in its scope description; the preserved search script actually matches 2512.20937, this exact title and RealChain, as its terms list shows.

contributions.method: Real-centric Envelope Modeling (REM): Manifold Boundary Reconstruction (MBR) uses feature/latent perturbations of VAE real-image reconstructions to make near-real examples; Envelope Estimation (EE) uses a binary/tangency boundary; Cross-Domain Consistency (CDC) aligns a frozen DINO anchor and adapted learner across clean/degraded views (§3, printed pp.229–232).
contributions.dataset: RealChain’s existing dataset role comprises 14,000 source images from real pools and six text-to-image generator families plus a Seedream image-to-image stratum. No removal or reassessment of the recognized dataset role is authorized.
contributions.benchmark: Separate ND/CD evaluation of real/fake detection across 50 intended operation chains and seven source/mode strata, with nine independent baselines, balanced accuracy and reported robustness comparisons (§4, Table 5).

question_matrix.question: The complete RealChain construction protocol.
question_matrix.finding: Section 4 separates RealChain from the REM method: collect 7,000 real images; generate 6,000 text-to-image samples and 1,000 image-to-image samples; evaluate clean No Degradation (ND) and random Chain Degradation (CD) outputs. Fifty chains each process 140 real and 140 synthetic images; operation outputs feed the next operation and only the final output is evaluated. These are a separately defined detection evaluation resource and protocol, not merely REM training examples.
question_matrix.limitations: The main chapter is complete but not a complete operational specification: only 20 chain examples are shown; full configurations, image assignments and source identifiers were not obtained. The version-pinned chain JSON attempt timed out with zero bytes.

question_matrix.question: Real and synthetic source-image counts.
question_matrix.finding: RealChain contains 7,000 real images plus 7,000 synthetic images, or 14,000 clean source samples. Six text-to-image generators each render the same designed set of 1,000 prompts, producing 6,000 samples; Seedream 4.0 image-to-image generation adds 1,000 samples. Fifty CD chains × (140 real + 140 fake) imply 14,000 final CD instances, not a stated 50 × 14,000 cross product.
question_matrix.limitations: The exact number of unique base images assigned across chains, repeat assignments, failed generations and intermediate stored-image totals are not specified or independently counted from archives.

question_matrix.question: The exact generator list and versions.
question_matrix.finding: The chapter names QwenImage, SDv3.5, Flux.1, Hunyuan 3.0, NanoBanana and Seedream 4.0 for text-to-image generation, plus Seedream 4.0 in image-to-image mode. This is six named generator families and seven source/mode strata. Reference 16 identifies NanoBanana with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image. Table 5 preserves the seven source/mode result pairs.
source_locators: §4.1, PDF p.9 / printed p.233; Table 5, PDF p.11 / printed p.235; refs.5,16,23,43,46,50
question_matrix.limitations: Exact checkpoints, API snapshots, generation seeds, sampling settings and hashes are not supplied in the reviewed main chapter or verified metadata. Seven strata must not be restated as seven distinct generator families.

question_matrix.question: Text-to-image versus image-to-image composition.
question_matrix.finding: Text-to-image: 1,000 prompts × six generators = 6,000 fake images. Image-to-image: 1,000 prompts rendered with Seedream 4.0 using real references for style transfer and local editing = 1,000 fake images. Table 5 reports a separate i2i stratum; REM balanced accuracy is 83.7 ND / 78.8 CD, versus DDA 80.4 / 65.9.
source_locators: §4.1, PDF p.9 / printed p.233; Table 5, PDF p.11 / printed p.235
question_matrix.limitations: Reference-image identities, edit extent, correspondence to real ND samples, masks and operation quotas are not specified. This wave does not change image scopes or forensic tasks on the basis of image-to-image content.

question_matrix.question: Open-source versus commercial generator sources.
question_matrix.finding: The paper classifies QwenImage, SDv3.5 and Flux.1 as open-source sources, and Hunyuan 3.0, NanoBanana and Seedream 4.0 as commercial sources. The six text-to-image strata each have 1,000 samples, with an additional 1,000-image Seedream image-to-image stratum.
source_locators: §4.1, PDF p.9 / printed p.233; pinned author README, Source Images
question_matrix.limitations: This records the authors’ source categorization, not an independent audit of each generator’s licensing or API availability. Source-mode overlap and content differences can confound open/commercial comparisons.

question_matrix.question: Image-content, prompt and provenance relationships.
question_matrix.finding: The real pool is sourced from MSCOCO, OpenImage-v7, Unsplash (printed as Unplash) and ImageNet. The 1,000 text-to-image prompts consist of 500 coarse and 500 fine prompts, rendered across six models. Image-to-image examples use real reference images and a separate stated set of 1,000 prompts. Saving each intermediate degradation output preserves a described chain of operations.
question_matrix.limitations: Real-source quotas, image identifiers, prompt texts, reference-parent links, semantic matching across real/fake pools, deduplication and individual chain lineage are not independently verified. Shared prompts can correlate generator strata, while unmatched real/fake content can induce semantic confounding.

question_matrix.question: The number and definitions of degradation chains.
question_matrix.finding: The chapter specifies 50 randomly generated chains. Figure 5 explicitly lists chains 01–10 and 41–50, including X → Crop → Facebook → Screenshot and TikTok → Baidu → Facebook → Sticker → Screenshot. The other 30 chain definitions are not enumerated in the main chapter. The public HF sibling listing includes degradation_chains.json, but its one pinned retrieval failed with HTTP 0 / curl 28 and zero body bytes.
source_locators: §4.2 and Fig.5, PDF pp.9–10 / printed pp.233–234; HF revision 0f0007d05cbd5ab6213783ad9ec3c2d38ab457c0 sibling metadata
question_matrix.limitations: Fifty configurations are a manuscript/README claim supported by partial examples, not 50 verified configuration bodies. No retry or alternate source was used to fill the gap.

question_matrix.question: Degradation-chain lengths and operation ordering.
question_matrix.finding: The main chapter constructs each chain from 1–3 propagation operations and 0–2 post-processing operations, implying a possible 1–5 total operations. Operations are ordered; each intermediate result becomes the next input and the final result is evaluated. The pinned README instead says length 2–5. Neither statement is silently substituted for the other.
source_locators: §4.2, PDF pp.9–10 / printed pp.233–234; Fig.5; README at c1e8aacf68f041d3abe6509dc01425c5e42ab01e, Chain Degradations
question_matrix.limitations: No fixed five-level severity schedule is defined. Exact sampling probabilities, ordering constraints, random seeds and whether a one-operation chain actually occurs are not verified. The inaccessible full JSON prevents reconciliation of paper versus README bounds.

question_matrix.question: Social-media platform simulations.
question_matrix.finding: Figure 5 uses six platform labels: X, Facebook, TikTok, WeChat, Baidu and Instagram. The operation library covers PC→PC, mobile→mobile, PC→mobile and mobile→PC upload/download routes, then filters, stickers, crops/aspect changes and screenshots. The README names WeChat, TikTok, Baidu, Instagram and X, omitting Facebook from its shorter list.
source_locators: §4.2 and Fig.5, PDF pp.9–10 / printed pp.233–234; pinned README, Propagation
question_matrix.limitations: Platform labels and example chains do not establish exact application versions, devices, codec parameters or faithful implementation of each service. The repository’s platform list is not a verified correction to the paper.

question_matrix.question: Whether platform effects are measured or only synthetically approximated.
question_matrix.finding: The paper calls the benchmark a realistic simulation and describes upload/download propagation operations. This is sufficient to identify the intended evaluation stressor, but not to verify empirical measurement of actual deployed platform transformations. No independently validated codec/device calibration is supplied in the reviewed source or fetched metadata.

current_authoritative_paper.abstract: The recent proliferation of photorealistic AIgenerated images (AIGI) has raised urgent concerns about their potential misuse, particularly on social media platforms. Current state-of-the-art AIGI detection methods typically rely on large, deep neural architectures, creating significant computational barriers to real-time, large-scale deployment on platforms like social media. To challenge this reliance on computationally intensive models, we introduce LAID, the first framework-to our knowledge-that benchmarks and evaluates the detection performance and efficiency of off-the-shelf lightweight neural networks. In this framework, we comprehensively train and evaluate selected models on a representative subset of the GenImage dataset across spatial, spectral, and fusion image domains. Our results demonstrate that lightweight models can achieve competitive accuracy, even under adversarial conditions, while incurring substantially lower memory and computation costs compared to current state-of-the-art methods. This study offers valuable insight into the trade-off between efficiency and performance in AIGI detection and lays a foundation for the development of practical, scalable, and trustworthy detection systems. The source code of LAID can be found at: https://github.com/nchivar/LAID.

Maintainer accepted retaining research_types method for curated:98977aa8b726ead071fe and detection under locked R2/R4; no R215 paper, taxonomy, evidence-provenance or metadata field is changed. The complete official CVF CVPR Workshops 2026 accepted manuscript (11 pages, printed 379-389; not CVPR Main) contributes Tunable Attention Pooling: trainable attention aggregates final patch and CLS features from a frozen VFM for a binary forensic classifier. Its separately stated comparative contribution is substantial and independently interpretable: Table 4 has 42 configurations, 15 encoders and six VFM families under a standardized frozen-encoder/linear-classifier recipe on existing OpenSDI. PE-G F1/accuracy 89.54/89.81 versus CLIP at336 75.63/77.45, and TAP achieves OpenSDI92.94/92.96. GenImage mean accuracy instead declines97.16 to95.67 with TAP; broad superiority is not assumed. The maintainer applies a conservative contribution-level R2 threshold: these standardized model-selection and comparative experiments supporting TAP, discussed in section4.2.1 under ablation/evaluation, do not clearly establish a separately contributed reusable benchmark framework. The competing permissive interpretation remains credible: the broad standardized comparison can itself qualify as a reusable systematic comparative framework and support method;benchmark. No new task, dataset, split registry, code release or placement outside an ablation section is a mandatory R2 condition; their absence alone does not reject benchmark. This is a bounded maintainer policy judgment with medium confidence, not proof of no reusable scientific value. Existing B1I evidence contains no clearly independent benchmark specification unconsidered by this rationale; the known comparison and framework counterargument are explicitly considered. Evidence: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026W/SAFE/papers/Abdullah_TAP_into_the_Patch_Tokens_Leveraging_Vision_Foundation_Model_Features_CVPRW_2026_paper.pdf; SHA256 f287854182676a679bde7ae3ce022fff0769b7ec792f3a31ec587125ccb558ec. contributions.method_preserved: Efficiency-aware lightweight detection framework and spatial/spectral evaluation pipeline; current method is not re-adjudicated.
contributions.benchmark_candidate: Systematic comparative framework intended to evaluate interchangeable existing lightweight architectures on common accuracy, resource, domain and perturbation conditions.
contributions.dataset: GenImage reuse; no new dataset contribution proposed.

question_matrix.question: Which lightweight architectures were compared?
question_matrix.answer: Ten selected off-the-shelf architectures plus two existing lightweight detection baselines are evaluated: ShuffleNet, EdgeNeXt, MobileNetV3, MobileViT, MobileViTV2, MnasNet, SqueezeNet, MobileNetV2, FastViT, RegNet, Ladevic et al. and SpottingDiffusion. Initialization variants are preserved in Table I.

question_matrix.question: Parameter counts and computational costs?
question_matrix.answer: Table I reports 1.2–4.3 million pretrained parameters and 0.04–0.70 GFLOPs for the ten selections. The two exception baselines are described as 13.46 GFLOPs (Ladevic) and 23M parameters (SpottingDiffusion). Table IV ratios use a different apparent basis; binary heads and profiling are visible in code, but exact historical reconciliation is unverified.

question_matrix.question: Spatial, spectral and fusion representations?
question_matrix.answer: Independent architecturally identical models operate on spatial RGB and zero-centered 2D FFT plots. The paper defines fusion success as either prediction matching ground truth; current code confirms this oracle union. It is not a deployable label-fusion accuracy rule. Code max-probability F1/AUROC uses a different scoring construction.

question_matrix.question: Relationship to GenImage?
question_matrix.answer: GenImage is reused, with approximately 1.33M natural and 1.35M synthetic images across eight generator sources. No new dataset classification is proposed.

question_matrix.question: Subset sampling and splits?
question_matrix.answer: The paper halves original GenImage test data into validation/test before random class-generator subsampling: 100,000 train, 16,000 validation and 16,000 test. The training example is 6,250 per class per generator. No frozen sample IDs or seed were verified.

question_matrix.question: Balance and generator test protocol?
question_matrix.answer: Intended equal class-generator sampling implies 50,000 real/50,000 fake training and 8,000/8,000 validation/test if equal sampling is followed. All eight generators are represented; no generator holdout or cross-dataset evaluation is established. Asset-level balance and duplicate/content overlap are unverified.

question_matrix.question: Standardized recipes?
question_matrix.answer: A common stated training recipe exists, with initialization exceptions for the two prior baselines. Pinned code instead uses CrossEntropyLoss, checkpointing/early stopping on validation loss, and default batch/validation counts of 64/12,500 rather than the paper’s BCE, accuracy-based selection and 512/16,000. These differences limit exact reproducibility.

question_matrix.question: Accuracy, efficiency, robustness metrics?
question_matrix.answer: Clean accuracy, F1 and AUROC; five attack-family accuracies; parameter/GFLOP counts, accuracy per Mparameter/MFLOP, ImageNet-derived efficiency selection and R-squared plots are supplied. End-to-end latency, energy and production throughput are not demonstrated.

question_matrix.question: Operating/resource constraints reproducible?
question_matrix.answer: Explicit resource limits, initialization variants, input size, hardware and some software versions enable partial reproduction. Eligibility OR versus AND language, catalog versus profiled resource denominators, FLOP/MAC conventions and unpinned library/run details remain unresolved.

question_matrix.question: Robustness perturbations controlled and consistent?
question_matrix.answer: Crop, Gaussian blur, Gaussian noise, JPEG and compound degradations have bounded ranges. Exact shared random draws, sequence ordering and seeds across all architectures are not verified. These are synthetic generic degradations rather than measured platform uploads or adaptive gradient attacks. Fusion is an oracle statistic.

question_matrix.question: Independently reusable framework?
question_matrix.answer: The independently intended contribution is an accuracy-scalability comparison framework with eligibility/ranking rules, common data/training recipe, spatial/spectral/perturbation axes and multiple efficiency/accuracy metrics, backed by public train/test recipes. It can compare detectors beyond a single new model; numerical and fusion-validity limitations remain.

question_matrix.question: Comparisons merely method selection?
question_matrix.answer: The competing reading is a model-selection study using an efficiency score and a simple detection pipeline on one reused dataset. Against this, the stated end product and actual experiments systematically compare twelve existing architectures rather than validate only one bespoke learned detector. Reuse does not depend on a particular LAID architecture.

question_matrix.question: New technical components?
question_matrix.answer: An efficiency-based selection score and combined spatial/spectral evaluation harness are technical components. The networks, pretrained initialization, FFT and baselines are established. R2 does not require a new network, new images or a separately packaged evaluation library; method is retained without re-review.

question_matrix.question: Scripts, splits, baseline settings released?
question_matrix.answer: The pinned author repository contains train.py/test.py, README and listed data/baseline helpers. Two recipe bodies were inspected without execution. No frozen split lists, package lock or license file is listed. A weights link is advertised but not retrieved; script availability does not certify a complete reproducible release.

question_matrix.question: Contradictory findings?
question_matrix.answer: Contradictions and limits include MnasNet failure, spectral collapse under perturbations, oracle fusion accuracy, weak blur robustness, negative efficiency-score correlation, inconsistent parameter/FLOP bases, eligibility wording, BCE/CE and checkpoint differences, and the paper’s Mp spectral notation and spatial-versus-spatial sentence. Printed values are preserved.

question_matrix.question: Future detectors independently evaluable?
question_matrix.answer: Future detectors can be inserted into the specified common comparative axes and public recipe structure, supporting an independently reusable framework under R2. Exact paper replication and deployable fusion are not certified. The provisional addition carries medium confidence and requires maintainer acceptance.

positive_R2_evidence: Explicit independently intended framework for comparing lightweight detectors, not only a new trained architecture.
Common model-resource eligibility, ranked architecture variants, reused data/splits, initialization and training setup, spatial/spectral conditions and five perturbation families.
Accuracy/efficiency metrics and multiple independent baselines expose strengths and failures rather than only a single winner.
Public pinned train/test recipes provide a way to evaluate future architectures, albeit with material paper/code discrepancies.
counterevidence_and_limits: All empirical results rely on one GenImage sample with all eight generators represented; no evaluated cross-generator holdout or cross-dataset transfer.
Efficiency score also performs model selection; an alternative interpretation is a method-selection experiment rather than a stand-alone benchmark.
Fusion accuracy is oracle correctness union using ground truth; no deployable decision-rule robustness is established by these values.
Exact sample membership, seed and leakage controls unverified; stochastic perturbations may not be identical across architectures.
Paper/code loss, checkpoint criterion and default count differences, resource denominator differences and incomplete license/environment specification limit reproduction.
MnasNet and attacked spectral failures, poor blur robustness and negative E correlation qualify headline scalability/robustness claims.

R2_assessment.reason: The actual contribution defines and implements a reusable comparative framework whose subjects are interchangeable established detectors under explicit resource, data, representation and robustness axes, rather than merely comparing a proposed network with competitors. This satisfies the systematic-comparative-framework limb of locked R2 without demanding new data or a standalone evaluation package. Defective fusion interpretation and reproduction limits qualify scientific validity and practical reuse, but do not erase the independently intended and specified clean/single-domain comparative framework.
R2_assessment.competing_interpretation: A conservative reading treats efficiency ranking and one-dataset results as method selection; a maintainer could decline a benchmark tag if the remaining protocol is judged too tied to LAID or too underspecified. This is a bounded R2 policy judgment, not title/abstract word matching.
R2_assessment.precedent_boundaries: Unlike merely transferring R215 standardized-comparison rejection, this paper makes the generic comparison structure its primary objective and supplies interchangeable-model recipes. R574 open-set splits and R400 cross-domain task are positive examples of independent protocol design, but their specific novelty is not a mandatory template for every framework.

questions.question: Actual spatial-model prediction output
questions.answer: test_attacked receives perturbed spatial tensors and computes img_outputs=spatial_model(img_images), followed by img_preds=argmax(img_outputs,dim=1) and softmax fake probability. The two output logits correspond to natural/synthetic binary labels; no generator identity is predicted.

questions.question: Actual spectral-model prediction output
questions.answer: The same perturbed spatial tensors are converted to NumPy, passed through the listed FFT conversion helpers, stacked and sent to spectral_model. freq_preds is argmax and freq_probs is softmax fake probability. Separate models are used in code, unlike the paper’s Mp notation in spectral Equations4–5.

questions.question: Is a joint or fused class prediction constructed?
questions.answer: No joint fused class variable or learned fused classifier is constructed in the inspected attack routine. fusion_prob is maximum of the two fake probabilities and is stored for F1/AUROC; fused accuracy is accumulated separately from an OR of correctness indicators. The scoring value is not itself a selected class in this routine.

questions.question: Does fusion require ground truth?
questions.answer: The published fusion accuracy explicitly references labels[i] in correct=(img_preds[i]==labels[i]) or (freq_preds[i]==labels[i]). This statistic depends on ground truth to decide correctness and cannot choose the correct model’s predicted class at inference without an independent decision rule. The maximum fake-probability score itself does not reference labels.

questions.question: Oracle upper bound or practical classifier?
questions.answer: The accuracy is an oracle correctness-union upper bound on choosing between two predictions for each labelled example. This can validly quantify error complementarity as an explicitly identified oracle statistic. The manuscript calls it decision-level fusion and uses it to support deployable robustness, without identifying an oracle upper bound; therefore those deployment interpretations are unsupported by this statistic. This does not invalidate all clean or single-domain results.

questions.question: What inference-time combination is implemented?
questions.answer: The routine computes a maximum fake-probability score for separate F1/AUROC accounting. It does not implement an OR or AND over predicted class labels, voting, probability averaging, confidence-based model selection or a learned fusion module for its reported fusion accuracy. BinaryF1Score is instantiated without an explicit threshold; the exact external-library default is not independently pinned here.

questions.question: Do evaluation success and inference scores differ?
questions.answer: Yes. fusion_acc uses label-dependent OR-correctness, whereas fusion_f1 and fusion_auc consume the maximum probability score with ground-truth targets through metric objects. They measure different constructions, so fusion accuracy is not shown to be the accuracy of the maximum-probability predictor. TableIII reports only the former accuracy statistic.

questions.question: Do Table III Fusion results correspond to executable code?
questions.answer: The read-only pinned test.py implements exactly the paper’s OR-correctness rule and prints fusion accuracy by attack, conceptually corresponding to TableIII. This is source-code verification, not an execution or numeric reproduction. No run receipt, paper-time checkpoint or exact paper source commit binds the printed values to this later repository snapshot. FastViT combined65.09% is spatial accuracy;90.91% is the printed oracle-union fusion accuracy.

questions.question: Required checkpoints and inference settings available?
questions.answer: README advertises an optional Google Drive weights link, but no weights were retrieved. The pinned tree contains no checkpoint blobs. test.py loads model_state_dict from .pth files, matches model names in filenames, and seeks paired <model>_img_checkpoint.pth/<model>_freq_checkpoint.pth. Required exact model weights, hashes, training sampling and attack helper details remain unverified. Public script presence does not certify executable paper reproduction.

questions.question: Can the evaluation protocol reproduce without label-dependent selection?
questions.answer: The clean and single-domain evaluation structure is conventional labelled evaluation and can define ground-truth-free predictions before scoring. The published fusion-accuracy statistic intrinsically uses label-dependent selection; its oracle upper-bound measurement can be repeated on labelled data, but a deployable fusion predictor cannot be recovered from that success criterion alone. The existing max-probability score could be evaluated as a separate predictor, but its accuracy is not the printed oracle statistic and no remediation or rerun is authorized.

fusion_implementation_review.oracle_claim_boundary: Do not call the oracle statistic meaningless or every paper result invalid. It is an informative labelled upper bound on error complementarity, but is not identified as such by the manuscript and cannot substantiate its deployable fusion claims.

questions.question: Actual spatial-model prediction output
questions.answer: test_attacked receives perturbed spatial tensors and computes img_outputs=spatial_model(img_images), followed by img_preds=argmax(img_outputs,dim=1) and softmax fake probability. The two output logits correspond to natural/synthetic binary labels; no generator identity is predicted.

questions.question: Actual spectral-model prediction output
questions.answer: The same perturbed spatial tensors are converted to NumPy, passed through the listed FFT conversion helpers, stacked and sent to spectral_model. freq_preds is argmax and freq_probs is softmax fake probability. Separate models are used in code, unlike the paper’s Mp notation in spectral Equations4–5.

questions.question: Is a joint or fused class prediction constructed?
questions.answer: No joint fused class variable or learned fused classifier is constructed in the inspected attack routine. fusion_prob is maximum of the two fake probabilities and is stored for F1/AUROC; fused accuracy is accumulated separately from an OR of correctness indicators. The scoring value is not itself a selected class in this routine.

questions.question: Does fusion require ground truth?
questions.answer: The published fusion accuracy explicitly references labels[i] in correct=(img_preds[i]==labels[i]) or (freq_preds[i]==labels[i]). This statistic depends on ground truth to decide correctness and cannot choose the correct model’s predicted class at inference without an independent decision rule. The maximum fake-probability score itself does not reference labels.

questions.question: Oracle upper bound or practical classifier?
questions.answer: The accuracy is an oracle correctness-union upper bound on choosing between two predictions for each labelled example. This can validly quantify error complementarity as an explicitly identified oracle statistic. The manuscript calls it decision-level fusion and uses it to support deployable robustness, without identifying an oracle upper bound; therefore those deployment interpretations are unsupported by this statistic. This does not invalidate all clean or single-domain results.

questions.question: What inference-time combination is implemented?
questions.answer: The routine computes a maximum fake-probability score for separate F1/AUROC accounting. It does not implement an OR or AND over predicted class labels, voting, probability averaging, confidence-based model selection or a learned fusion module for its reported fusion accuracy. BinaryF1Score is instantiated without an explicit threshold; the exact external-library default is not independently pinned here.

questions.question: Do evaluation success and inference scores differ?
questions.answer: Yes. fusion_acc uses label-dependent OR-correctness, whereas fusion_f1 and fusion_auc consume the maximum probability score with ground-truth targets through metric objects. They measure different constructions, so fusion accuracy is not shown to be the accuracy of the maximum-probability predictor. TableIII reports only the former accuracy statistic.

questions.question: Do Table III Fusion results correspond to executable code?
questions.answer: The read-only pinned test.py implements exactly the paper’s OR-correctness rule and prints fusion accuracy by attack, conceptually corresponding to TableIII. This is source-code verification, not an execution or numeric reproduction. No run receipt, paper-time checkpoint or exact paper source commit binds the printed values to this later repository snapshot. FastViT combined65.09% is spatial accuracy;90.91% is the printed oracle-union fusion accuracy.

questions.question: Required checkpoints and inference settings available?
questions.answer: README advertises an optional Google Drive weights link, but no weights were retrieved. The pinned tree contains no checkpoint blobs. test.py loads model_state_dict from .pth files, matches model names in filenames, and seeks paired <model>_img_checkpoint.pth/<model>_freq_checkpoint.pth. Required exact model weights, hashes, training sampling and attack helper details remain unverified. Public script presence does not certify executable paper reproduction.

questions.question: Can the evaluation protocol reproduce without label-dependent selection?
questions.answer: The clean and single-domain evaluation structure is conventional labelled evaluation and can define ground-truth-free predictions before scoring. The published fusion-accuracy statistic intrinsically uses label-dependent selection; its oracle upper-bound measurement can be repeated on labelled data, but a deployable fusion predictor cannot be recovered from that success criterion alone. The existing max-probability score could be evaluated as a separate predictor, but its accuracy is not the printed oracle statistic and no remediation or rerun is authorized.

fusion_rule_source.oracle_claim_boundary: Do not call the oracle statistic meaningless or every paper result invalid. It is an informative labelled upper bound on error complementarity, but is not identified as such by the manuscript and cannot substantiate its deployable fusion claims.

current_authoritative_paper.abstract: The recent proliferation of photorealistic AIgenerated images (AIGI) has raised urgent concerns about their potential misuse, particularly on social media platforms. Current state-of-the-art AIGI detection methods typically rely on large, deep neural architectures, creating significant computational barriers to real-time, large-scale deployment on platforms like social media. To challenge this reliance on computationally intensive models, we introduce LAID, the first framework-to our knowledge-that benchmarks and evaluates the detection performance and efficiency of off-the-shelf lightweight neural networks. In this framework, we comprehensively train and evaluate selected models on a representative subset of the GenImage dataset across spatial, spectral, and fusion image domains. Our results demonstrate that lightweight models can achieve competitive accuracy, even under adversarial conditions, while incurring substantially lower memory and computation costs compared to current state-of-the-art methods. This study offers valuable insight into the trade-off between efficiency and performance in AIGI detection and lays a foundation for the development of practical, scalable, and trustworthy detection systems. The source code of LAID can be found at: https://github.com/nchivar/LAID.

PE-G F1/accuracy 89.54/89.81 versus CLIP at336 75.63/77.45, and TAP achieves OpenSDI92.94/92.96. GenImage mean accuracy instead declines97.16 to95.67 with TAP; broad superiority is not assumed. The maintainer applies a conservative contribution-level R2 threshold: these standardized model-selection and comparative experiments supporting TAP, discussed in section4.2.1 under ablation/evaluation, do not clearly establish a separately contributed reusable benchmark framework. The competing permissive interpretation remains credible: the broad standardized comparison can itself qualify as a reusable systematic comparative framework and support method;benchmark. No new task, dataset, split registry, code release or placement outside an ablation section is a mandatory R2 condition; their absence alone does not reject benchmark. This is a bounded maintainer policy judgment with medium confidence, not proof of no reusable scientific value. Existing B1I evidence contains no clearly independent benchmark specification unconsidered by this rationale; the known comparison and framework counterargument are explicitly considered. Evidence: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026W/SAFE/papers/Abdullah_TAP_into_the_Patch_Tokens_Leveraging_Vision_Foundation_Model_Features_CVPRW_2026_paper.pdf; SHA256 f287854182676a679bde7ae3ce022fff0769b7ec792f3a31ec587125ccb558ec. source.version: arXiv 2507.05162v1 author manuscript, submitted 7 July 2025 16:18:19 UTC; PDF margin dated7 July2025. Comment says to appear PST2025.
source.title: LAID: Lightweight AI-Generated Image Detection in Spatial and Spectral Domains
source.identity_verification: Exact title and both authors agree with canonical record. arXiv landing links author repository and identifies intended PST2025 work. DOI redirects to IEEE document11268874 but returned zero-byte HTTP202; no final manuscript identity or byte equivalence is certified. Canonical arxiv_id remains empty; it is not edited.
source.text_extraction_limitation: Pypdf layout extraction warns about rotated text; critical table/formula pages5–9 were rendered and inspected visually; plain extraction provides complementary order.

local_search.method: rg --files --hidden, .git excluded, targeted filename patterns; local intake/ledger/source identity text searched before network.

contributions.method_preserved: Efficiency-aware lightweight detection framework and spatial/spectral evaluation pipeline; current method is not re-adjudicated.
contributions.benchmark_candidate: Systematic comparative framework intended to evaluate interchangeable existing lightweight architectures on common accuracy, resource, domain and perturbation conditions.
contributions.dataset: GenImage reuse; no new dataset contribution proposed.

question_matrix.question: Which lightweight architectures were compared?
question_matrix.answer: Ten selected off-the-shelf architectures plus two existing lightweight detection baselines are evaluated: ShuffleNet, EdgeNeXt, MobileNetV3, MobileViT, MobileViTV2, MnasNet, SqueezeNet, MobileNetV2, FastViT, RegNet, Ladevic et al. and SpottingDiffusion. Initialization variants are preserved in Table I.

question_matrix.question: Parameter counts and computational costs?
question_matrix.answer: Table I reports 1.2–4.3 million pretrained parameters and 0.04–0.70 GFLOPs for the ten selections. The two exception baselines are described as 13.46 GFLOPs (Ladevic) and 23M parameters (SpottingDiffusion). Table IV ratios use a different apparent basis; binary heads and profiling are visible in code, but exact historical reconciliation is unverified.

question_matrix.question: Spatial, spectral and fusion representations?
question_matrix.answer: Independent architecturally identical models operate on spatial RGB and zero-centered 2D FFT plots. The paper defines fusion success as either prediction matching ground truth; current code confirms this oracle union. It is not a deployable label-fusion accuracy rule. Code max-probability F1/AUROC uses a different scoring construction.

question_matrix.question: Relationship to GenImage?
question_matrix.answer: GenImage is reused, with approximately 1.33M natural and 1.35M synthetic images across eight generator sources. No new dataset classification is proposed.

question_matrix.question: Subset sampling and splits?
question_matrix.answer: The paper halves original GenImage test data into validation/test before random class-generator subsampling: 100,000 train, 16,000 validation and 16,000 test. The training example is 6,250 per class per generator. No frozen sample IDs or seed were verified.

question_matrix.question: Balance and generator test protocol?
question_matrix.answer: Intended equal class-generator sampling implies 50,000 real/50,000 fake training and 8,000/8,000 validation/test if equal sampling is followed. All eight generators are represented; no generator holdout or cross-dataset evaluation is established. Asset-level balance and duplicate/content overlap are unverified.

question_matrix.question: Standardized recipes?
question_matrix.answer: A common stated training recipe exists, with initialization exceptions for the two prior baselines. Pinned code instead uses CrossEntropyLoss, checkpointing/early stopping on validation loss, and default batch/validation counts of 64/12,500 rather than the paper’s BCE, accuracy-based selection and 512/16,000. These differences limit exact reproducibility.

question_matrix.question: Accuracy, efficiency, robustness metrics?
question_matrix.answer: Clean accuracy, F1 and AUROC; five attack-family accuracies; parameter/GFLOP counts, accuracy per Mparameter/MFLOP, ImageNet-derived efficiency selection and R-squared plots are supplied. End-to-end latency, energy and production throughput are not demonstrated.

question_matrix.question: Operating/resource constraints reproducible?
question_matrix.answer: Explicit resource limits, initialization variants, input size, hardware and some software versions enable partial reproduction. Eligibility OR versus AND language, catalog versus profiled resource denominators, FLOP/MAC conventions and unpinned library/run details remain unresolved.

question_matrix.question: Robustness perturbations controlled and consistent?
question_matrix.answer: Crop, Gaussian blur, Gaussian noise, JPEG and compound degradations have bounded ranges. Exact shared random draws, sequence ordering and seeds across all architectures are not verified. These are synthetic generic degradations rather than measured platform uploads or adaptive gradient attacks. Fusion is an oracle statistic.

question_matrix.question: Independently reusable framework?
question_matrix.answer: The independently intended contribution is an accuracy-scalability comparison framework with eligibility/ranking rules, common data/training recipe, spatial/spectral/perturbation axes and multiple efficiency/accuracy metrics, backed by public train/test recipes. It can compare detectors beyond a single new model; numerical and fusion-validity limitations remain.

question_matrix.question: Comparisons merely method selection?
question_matrix.answer: The competing reading is a model-selection study using an efficiency score and a simple detection pipeline on one reused dataset. Against this, the stated end product and actual experiments systematically compare twelve existing architectures rather than validate only one bespoke learned detector. Reuse does not depend on a particular LAID architecture.

question_matrix.question: New technical components?
question_matrix.answer: An efficiency-based selection score and combined spatial/spectral evaluation harness are technical components. The networks, pretrained initialization, FFT and baselines are established. R2 does not require a new network, new images or a separately packaged evaluation library; method is retained without re-review.

question_matrix.question: Scripts, splits, baseline settings released?
question_matrix.answer: The pinned author repository contains train.py/test.py, README and listed data/baseline helpers. Two recipe bodies were inspected without execution. No frozen split lists, package lock or license file is listed. A weights link is advertised but not retrieved; script availability does not certify a complete reproducible release.

question_matrix.question: Contradictory findings?
question_matrix.answer: Contradictions and limits include MnasNet failure, spectral collapse under perturbations, oracle fusion accuracy, weak blur robustness, negative efficiency-score correlation, inconsistent parameter/FLOP bases, eligibility wording, BCE/CE and checkpoint differences, and the paper’s Mp spectral notation and spatial-versus-spatial sentence. Printed values are preserved.

question_matrix.question: Future detectors independently evaluable?
question_matrix.answer: Future detectors can be inserted into the specified common comparative axes and public recipe structure, supporting an independently reusable framework under R2. Exact paper replication and deployable fusion are not certified. The provisional addition carries medium confidence and requires maintainer acceptance.

protocol.task: Binary synthetic-image authenticity detection: M_theta(I)→{0natural,1synthetic}; not source attribution.

model_selection.eligibility: SectionIV-A says at least one of parameters<10M OR FLOPs<1G; SectionV-C/TableI caption describe parameter AND FLOP filtering. All ten selected entries satisfy both printed limits, so their membership is unaffected, but candidate universe rule is not silently harmonized.
model_selection.sources: PyTorch hub and timm pretrained model libraries; no model downloads or Hugging Face dataset operations performed by reviewer.
model_selection.rank_selection: Top10 after parent-architecture deduplication, based on ImageNet1K top1 accuracy and resource score. Two existing lightweight detection baselines are exceptions to eligibility criteria.
model_selection.new_technical_components: An explicit efficiency score/model-selection protocol and spatial/spectral experiment harness; pretrained architectures and FFT are existing techniques, no novel learned architecture required for R2.

data.existing_resource: GenImage reused; no new dataset claim
data.split_construction: Original GenImage test set first divided evenly into validation and test; then random subsampling across class-generator pairs. Training example specifies6,250 natural and6,250 synthetic per generator subset.
data.balance_and_derived_counts: Intended equal16 class-generator strata implies50,000/50,000 train and8,000/8,000 validation/test; derived per-pair val/test1000 if equally balanced. Exact IDs and actual asset-level class counts not inspected.
data.generator_holdout: All eight generator subsets sampled; no independently evaluated generator holdout or cross-dataset test. Cross-generator generalization is future work (§VII), not an established result.
data.leakage: No exact content/prompt/source deduplication or source-image grouping safeguards demonstrated. GenImage real images repeated across generator directories or near-duplicate content could confound random splitting; actual overlap not measured.

representations.spectral: zero-centered2D FFT plots derived from matching spatial images; independently trained architecturally-identical model
representations.fusion: Oracle correctness union under perturbed testing; not a verified inference-time fusion predictor. Clean fusion not tabulated because authors report little advantage.
representations.preprocessing: Paper states normalize spatial/spectral to[0,255], resize256×256, storePyTorch tensors; exact FFT plot scaling/log mapping and helper contents not inspected.

paper_training.initialization: ImageNet1K pretrained; Ladevic baseline random, SpottingDiffusion pretrainedMobileNetV2 backbone withotherparameters random

code_training_differences.loss: Pinned train.py399 uses nn.CrossEntropyLoss, not printed BCE
code_training_differences.checkpoint: Pinned train.py346–350 compares val_loss<best_val_loss, not validation accuracy; comment incorrectly says accuracy
code_training_differences.defaults: batch64 andval_image_count12500; paper512 and16000. CLI can override, but exact paper run command/config is not archived.
code_training_differences.scheduler: Steps on validation loss; no random seed setting in inspected train/test scripts; helper randomness remains uninspected.

perturbations.noise: Gaussian noise variance uniformly5–20, as printed; not reinterpreted as standard deviation
perturbations.combined: Each individual transformation applied with50% probability; order, realized draws and whether identical across every model are not established from paper/inspected recipes.
perturbations.threat_model: Generic stochastic image degradations, not gradient-based adaptive adversarial attacks; intended social-media simulations, no actual platform-upload study.

metrics.resources: Parameters/GFLOPs andaccuracy perMparameter/MFLOP; no throughput, latency, energy or peak memory independently measured.
metrics.efficiency_basis_boundary: TableI pretrained catalog counts andTableIV post-fine-tuning efficiency ratios are not numerically interchangeable. Code replaces binary heads andprofilesactualexampleviaTHOP, offeringa plausiblebasisdifference, but exact historicalrun/config andFLOP-vsMAC convention not certified; preserve allprinted values.

protocol.environment: NVIDIA A100, Intel Xeon Platinum8362,128GBmemory;Python3.12.4,PyTorch2.1.2,CUDA12.1 asreported. Libraryversions for torchvision/timm/THOP, all resource timing parameters, seed/multiple-run uncertainty notspecified.

Table I.measurement_status: Printed manuscript values transcribed; no experiment rerun or source-value correction.

Table II.measurement_status: Printed manuscript values transcribed; no experiment rerun or source-value correction.

Table III.fusion_warning: Paper and current author code count a sample correct if either model prediction equals ground truth; this is oracle correctness union, not a specified deployable prediction rule. Preserve printed values without reinterpreting them as deployable fusion accuracy.

Table IV.measurement_status: Printed manuscript values transcribed; no experiment rerun or source-value correction.

Figure 4.causal_inference: No architectural causal effect or out-of-sample selection guarantee established.

release_review.repository_identity: Author-linked in complete manuscript and exact-title README; README cites arXiv2507.05162 and PST2025.

license.conclusion: No explicit repository license was found in pinned tree/metadata; do not infer code or dataset licensing from public visibility.

release_review.split_release: No frozen sample-ID/split-list file appears in the pinned ten-entry recursive tree. Generation helper is listed; contents and sampled data were not retrieved. Recipe can create a local sampled dataset but exact paper sample membership and randomness cannot be certified.
release_review.reproduction_status: README and two executable recipe bodies are publicly readable, but no package lock/requirements file, complete evaluation manifests, dataset bodies or checkpoints verified. No code executed; no independent numerical reproduction.

positive_R2_evidence: Explicit independently intended framework for comparing lightweight detectors, not only a new trained architecture.
Common model-resource eligibility, ranked architecture variants, reused data/splits, initialization and training setup, spatial/spectral conditions and five perturbation families.
Accuracy/efficiency metrics and multiple independent baselines expose strengths and failures rather than only a single winner.
Public pinned train/test recipes provide a way to evaluate future architectures, albeit with material paper/code discrepancies.
counterevidence_and_limits: All empirical results rely on one GenImage sample with all eight generators represented; no evaluated cross-generator holdout or cross-dataset transfer.
Efficiency score also performs model selection; an alternative interpretation is a method-selection experiment rather than a stand-alone benchmark.
Fusion accuracy is oracle correctness union using ground truth; no deployable decision-rule robustness is established by these values.
Exact sample membership, seed and leakage controls unverified; stochastic perturbations may not be identical across architectures.
Paper/code loss, checkpoint criterion and default count differences, resource denominator differences and incomplete license/environment specification limit reproduction.
MnasNet and attacked spectral failures, poor blur robustness and negative E correlation qualify headline scalability/robustness claims.

R2_assessment.reason: The actual contribution defines and implements a reusable comparative framework whose subjects are interchangeable established detectors under explicit resource, data, representation and robustness axes, rather than merely comparing a proposed network with competitors. This satisfies the systematic-comparative-framework limb of locked R2 without demanding new data or a standalone evaluation package. Defective fusion interpretation and reproduction limits qualify scientific validity and practical reuse, but do not erase the independently intended and specified clean/single-domain comparative framework.
R2_assessment.competing_interpretation: A conservative reading treats efficiency ranking and one-dataset results as method selection; a maintainer could decline a benchmark tag if the remaining protocol is judged too tied to LAID or too underspecified. This is a bounded R2 policy judgment, not title/abstract word matching.
R2_assessment.precedent_boundaries: Unlike merely transferring R215 standardized-comparison rejection, this paper makes the generic comparison structure its primary objective and supplies interchangeable-model recipes. R574 open-set splits and R400 cross-domain task are positive examples of independent protocol design, but their specific novelty is not a mandatory template for every framework.

confidence.R2_benchmark_contribution: Medium; complete primary manuscript and read-only pinned recipes establish intended reusable comparison, with real model-selection counterinterpretation.
confidence.source_identity: High for pinned author v1; publisher-final equivalence unverified.
confidence.numerical_and_reproduction: No rerun; serious oracle-fusion interpretation and paper/code differences prevent certification of deployable robustness or faithful reproduction.

questions.question: Actual spatial-model prediction output
questions.answer: test_attacked receives perturbed spatial tensors and computes img_outputs=spatial_model(img_images), followed by img_preds=argmax(img_outputs,dim=1) and softmax fake probability. The two output logits correspond to natural/synthetic binary labels; no generator identity is predicted.

questions.question: Actual spectral-model prediction output
questions.answer: The same perturbed spatial tensors are converted to NumPy, passed through the listed FFT conversion helpers, stacked and sent to spectral_model. freq_preds is argmax and freq_probs is softmax fake probability. Separate models are used in code, unlike the paper’s Mp notation in spectral Equations4–5.

questions.question: Is a joint or fused class prediction constructed?
questions.answer: No joint fused class variable or learned fused classifier is constructed in the inspected attack routine. fusion_prob is maximum of the two fake probabilities and is stored for F1/AUROC; fused accuracy is accumulated separately from an OR of correctness indicators. The scoring value is not itself a selected class in this routine.

questions.question: Does fusion require ground truth?
questions.answer: The published fusion accuracy explicitly references labels[i] in correct=(img_preds[i]==labels[i]) or (freq_preds[i]==labels[i]). This statistic depends on ground truth to decide correctness and cannot choose the correct model’s predicted class at inference without an independent decision rule. The maximum fake-probability score itself does not reference labels.

questions.question: Oracle upper bound or practical classifier?
questions.answer: The accuracy is an oracle correctness-union upper bound on choosing between two predictions for each labelled example. This can validly quantify error complementarity as an explicitly identified oracle statistic. The manuscript calls it decision-level fusion and uses it to support deployable robustness, without identifying an oracle upper bound; therefore those deployment interpretations are unsupported by this statistic. This does not invalidate all clean or single-domain results.

questions.question: What inference-time combination is implemented?
questions.answer: The routine computes a maximum fake-probability score for separate F1/AUROC accounting. It does not implement an OR or AND over predicted class labels, voting, probability averaging, confidence-based model selection or a learned fusion module for its reported fusion accuracy. BinaryF1Score is instantiated without an explicit threshold; the exact external-library default is not independently pinned here.

questions.question: Do evaluation success and inference scores differ?
questions.answer: Yes. fusion_acc uses label-dependent OR-correctness, whereas fusion_f1 and fusion_auc consume the maximum probability score with ground-truth targets through metric objects. They measure different constructions, so fusion accuracy is not shown to be the accuracy of the maximum-probability predictor. TableIII reports only the former accuracy statistic.

questions.question: Do Table III Fusion results correspond to executable code?
questions.answer: The read-only pinned test.py implements exactly the paper’s OR-correctness rule and prints fusion accuracy by attack, conceptually corresponding to TableIII. This is source-code verification, not an execution or numeric reproduction. No run receipt, paper-time checkpoint or exact paper source commit binds the printed values to this later repository snapshot. FastViT combined65.09% is spatial accuracy;90.91% is the printed oracle-union fusion accuracy.

questions.question: Required checkpoints and inference settings available?
questions.answer: README advertises an optional Google Drive weights link, but no weights were retrieved. The pinned tree contains no checkpoint blobs. test.py loads model_state_dict from .pth files, matches model names in filenames, and seeks paired <model>_img_checkpoint.pth/<model>_freq_checkpoint.pth. Required exact model weights, hashes, training sampling and attack helper details remain unverified. Public script presence does not certify executable paper reproduction.

questions.question: Can the evaluation protocol reproduce without label-dependent selection?
questions.answer: The clean and single-domain evaluation structure is conventional labelled evaluation and can define ground-truth-free predictions before scoring. The published fusion-accuracy statistic intrinsically uses label-dependent selection; its oracle upper-bound measurement can be repeated on labelled data, but a deployable fusion predictor cannot be recovered from that success criterion alone. The existing max-probability score could be evaluated as a separate predictor, but its accuracy is not the printed oracle statistic and no remediation or rerun is authorized.

fusion_rule_source.oracle_claim_boundary: Do not call the oracle statistic meaningless or every paper result invalid. It is an informative labelled upper bound on error complementarity, but is not identified as such by the manuscript and cannot substantiate its deployable fusion claims.

R034 accepted under locked R2: RealChain is an independently specified reusable detector-evaluation benchmark/protocol/resource, distinct from REM and its retained dataset role. The complete ECCV 2026 publisher chapter defines 7,000 real and 7,000 synthetic sources, seven source/mode strata, 50 degradation chains, ND/CD settings, Balanced Accuracy and nine independent baselines. Add benchmark; retain method, dataset, detection and fully_generated. Contribution confidence high; reproducibility confidence medium. Complete chain definitions, timed-out JSON, archive contents, splits, evaluator and numerical reproduction remain unverified. Preserve nonuniform REM superiority, DRCT table discrepancies, backbone/average ambiguity and CDC ablation inconsistency. OUT_OF_SCOPE_BIBLIOGRAPHIC_VERSION_OBSERVATION remains separate; P034 and all canonical bibliographic fields remain pending and unchanged. ECCV publisher DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-37429-5_14, sections 4-5, Tables 1 and 5: RealChain ND/CD Balanced Accuracy REM 92.4/84.2 versus DDA 88.8/65.8; CD gap 18.4 percentage points. The benchmark has 7,000 real plus 7,000 synthetic source images, seven source/mode strata, 50 chains each processing 140 real and 140 fake, and nine independent baselines. Not a 50-times-full-corpus cross product. Full chain configuration/splits/archive/evaluator and independent reproduction unverified; timed-out JSON preserved. Git c1e8aacf68f041d3abe6509dc01425c5e42ab01e; HF 0f0007d05cbd5ab6213783ad9ec3c2d38ab457c0. Bibliographic version differences remain outside this R2 correction; P034 pending. Publisher source https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/978-3-032-37429-5_14.pdf; SHA256 ee8012fd5021f6ac40f9fc336f81d94e2d734630bface9c333d37cc975e49fe9. Early arXiv 2512.20937v1 abstract has 12 authors, eight evaluations and 7.5% reported average improvement; publisher has 13 authors including Manni Cui, twelve evaluations and 6.9%. Do not merge these versions or infer exact construction changes from the early abstract. Preserve canonical authors, DOI, year, venue, title and bibliographic provenance; no terminal P034 decision. No tasks, scopes, publications, authors, institutions, inclusion or relationships change. Exactly this original research-type action closes after the approved correction. Terminal no_action_after_review means no further work remains for the accepted bounded correction, not that no data changed. All original evidence and retrieval timestamps are preserved.

decisions.title: LAID: Lightweight AI-Generated Image Detection in Spatial and Spectral Domains
decisions.review_note: Batch B review R359; BENCHMARK_ADDITION_SUPPORTED; PROPOSE_CORRECTION_ACCEPTED. Maintainer accepts method to method;benchmark for curated:e688194977fa7bbf7db3. R359 accepted under locked R2: LAID contributes a separately intended model-independent comparative framework with architecture eligibility/resource constraints, reusable training/testing interfaces, spatial/FFT inputs, standardized recipes, GenImage sampling, joint accuracy/resource measures and controlled postprocessing evaluations. This exceeds ordinary model selection and differs from bounded R215; model count alone is insufficient. Add benchmark; retain method, detection and fully_generated; no dataset or analysis_study. curated:aa7dceb70828cdd6ad39.title: Beyond Artifacts: Real-Centric Envelope Modeling for Reliable AI-Generated Image Detection
curated:aa7dceb70828cdd6ad39.authors: Ruiqi Liu; Yi Han; Zhengbo Zhang; Liwei Yao; Zhiyuan Yan; Jialiang Shen; Zhijin Chen; Boyi Sun; Lubin Weng; Jing Dong; Yan Wang; Shu Wu
curated:aa7dceb70828cdd6ad39.abstract: The rapid progress of generative models has intensified the need for reliable and robust detection under real-world conditions. However, existing detectors often overfit to generator-specific artifacts and remain highly sensitive to real-world degradations. As generative architectures evolve and images undergo multi-round cross-platform sharing and post-processing (chain degradations), these artifact cues become obsolete and harder to detect. To address this, we propose Real-centric Envelope Modeling (REM), a new paradigm that shifts detection from learning generator artifacts to modeling the robust distribution of real images. REM introduces feature-level perturbations in self-reconstruction to generate near-real samples, and employs an envelope estimator with cross-domain consistency to learn a boundary enclosing the real image manifold. We further build RealChain, a comprehensive benchmark covering both open-source and commercial generators with simulated real-world degradation. Across eight benchmark evaluations, REM achieves an average improvement of 7.5% over state-of-the-art methods, and notably maintains exceptional generalization on the severely degraded RealChain benchmark, establishing a solid foundation for synthetic image detection under real-world conditions. The code and the RealChain benchmark will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the paper.

curated:e688194977fa7bbf7db3.title: LAID: Lightweight AI-Generated Image Detection in Spatial and Spectral Domains
curated:e688194977fa7bbf7db3.venue: Annual International Conference on Privacy, Security, and Trust
curated:e688194977fa7bbf7db3.venue_name: Annual International Conference on Privacy, Security, and Trust
curated:e688194977fa7bbf7db3.raw_venue: Annual International Conference on Privacy, Security, and Trust
curated:e688194977fa7bbf7db3.abstract: The recent proliferation of photorealistic AIgenerated images (AIGI) has raised urgent concerns about their potential misuse, particularly on social media platforms. Current state-of-the-art AIGI detection methods typically rely on large, deep neural architectures, creating significant computational barriers to real-time, large-scale deployment on platforms like social media. To challenge this reliance on computationally intensive models, we introduce LAID, the first framework-to our knowledge-that benchmarks and evaluates the detection performance and efficiency of off-the-shelf lightweight neural networks. In this framework, we comprehensively train and evaluate selected models on a representative subset of the GenImage dataset across spatial, spectral, and fusion image domains. Our results demonstrate that lightweight models can achieve competitive accuracy, even under adversarial conditions, while incurring substantially lower memory and computation costs compared to current state-of-the-art methods. This study offers valuable insight into the trade-off between efficiency and performance in AIGI detection and lays a foundation for the development of practical, scalable, and trustworthy detection systems. The source code of LAID can be found at: https://github.com/nchivar/LAID.
